title: Apple Reportedly Apologizes Over Hacking Of Some Chinese Accounts
text:
Shutterstock photo
( RTTNews.com ) - Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) apologized over the hacking of some Chinese accounts in phishing scams, almost a week after it emerged that stolen Apple IDs had been used to swipe customer funds, the Wall Street Journal reported.
Apple reportedly said it found "a small number of our users' accounts" had been accessed through phishing scams.
Apple reportedly said that the affected accounts were not secured with two-factor authentication. This allowed criminals to phish for account credentials and then extract money using apps like Alipay.
If two-factor authentication is enabled, users must independently approve account access for new device logins. This greatly reduces the chance of phishing attacks ultimately working, as unknown login requests can simply be denied.
